defect_observations.observation: The first uniqueness clause ("so its law identifies lambda uniquely") does not by itself exclude another mixing law; uniqueness rests on the compressed specialization of thm:p15-directing-law-uniqueness to S={0,1} (and independently on the threshold argument at annex 480-489).
Weak convergence of real laws is applied to a polynomial integrand; a bounded continuous extension off [0,1] is implicit (all laws live on [0,1]).

The identification step reuses "the measurable-section strong-law argument used for the Polya mixture" by reference (PA 100-111) instead of restating it; that argument is independent of the beta parameter law.
Triviality of the limit field is taken from the reverse-average Hewitt-Savage theorem, whereas Durrett Example 4.7.4 (p.251) invokes Theorem 2.5.4; the route is otherwise the source route.
The body says the common countable determining class is proved in the annex; the proof is in the C011 annex item (A 291-299), not the C010 item.
Wording: the Exercise 4.7.4 part is proved from the truncated conditional-product identity (A 495-509), not from the symmetrization identity named in the body.
Exercise 4.7.3 is displayed as binom(N-k,m-k)/binom(N,m); Durrett p.255 displays binom(n-k,n-m)/binom(n,m). Equal by binomial symmetry (both vanish for m<k); the equivalence is not stated.

Unlike C006 and C017, the entry does not cross-reference its worked boundary thm:p15-w02b-p15-022-projection-boundary (WB 957-986); C001, C002 and C009 likewise have their worked boundaries only in other on-route entries without a pointer from the entry.
